title: An MI300X Over MCP: What the Matrix Cores Execute, and What They Don't
why_read: A hands-on hardware inventory of AMD's MI300X GPU numeric format performance, built through a custom MCP tool server, gives concrete real-world benchmark numbers not found in vendor spec sheets.
analysis: This post measures actual throughput of different numeric formats (fp8 e4m3fnuz, int8, and the absence of fp4) on a rented AMD Instinct MI300X GPU, finding fp8 running 1.77x faster than bf16 while int8 runs slower than expected despite AMD rating it equivalently to fp8. The author built a small set of Python MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools to remotely manage and query the rented GPU droplet, using this tooling as the mechanism for gathering hardware truth rather than trusting spec sheets. This kind of empirical hardware characterization is valuable because vendor-published numbers often don't match real achievable throughput, and discrepancies here directly matter for anyone choosing numeric formats for inference or training on AMD hardware. The MCP-as-remote-hardware-interface angle is also a mildly novel practical pattern, though the core value is the empirical benchmark data itself.
